scenes.say: Ever wonder how Go interfaces just work—without any explicit implements keyword?

scenes.label: Interface
scenes.sub: Any type that implements the methods is an interface—no declaration needed.
scenes.say: In Go, if a type has all the methods an interface requires, it satisfies that interface automatically.
Here, File defines a Read method. That means File implicitly satisfies the Reader interface—no extra code needed.
This makes your code flexible, decoupled, and simple. You can swap implementations without changing interface code.

scenes.question: How do you declare a type implements an interface?
scenes.right: Just by matching the interface's methods—no keyword needed.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this: Go doesn't need an explicit implements keyword. Just match the interface's methods and you're done.
